key_insight: TWICE isolates decision credit from sampling luck by comparing factual and counterfactual agent episodes that share downstream noise.
engineering_relevance: For agentic search with deterministic retrieval and grading, shared-noise rollouts can make policy-gradient credit assignment more precise and token-efficient.
method: Key token-level Gumbel noise by turn and line so counterfactual twins inherit the factual episode’s downstream noise.
Convert paired outcome differences into turn-level advantages for actor-sampled policy-gradient updates; deploy only the actor.
Allocate the twin-rollout budget using a square-root rule based on predicted outcome disagreement and cost.
evidence_signal: Across seven question-answering benchmarks, TWICE improves average exact match over GRPO by 5.3 points on Qwen2.5-3B and 4.5 points on 7B, while using 68% fewer auxiliary tokens than VinePPO.
watch_item: Variance reduction depends on twin outcome correlation, and stochastic tools or environments may complicate faithful shared-noise coupling.
paper_title: Same Luck, Different Choice: Twin-World Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
